answer: Entry is anchored to a settled contract, not a deposit. Before earning, an identity presents one completed external contract whose counterparty already paid and has not disputed for thirty days; the hash is consumed on use, so it cannot back two identities, and the payer must hold ledger history older than the applicant. The anchor is priced by its value: it must be worth at least forty times the epoch emission the identity claims, so n shells need n real paying counterparties at that size. A comet needs a nadir it truly reached; an inlet, water already flowing.
